question: In chapter 7’s education discussion on physical page 200, how are household expenses received by public schools treated, and why are uniforms or books paid to private sellers excluded?
answer:
Out-of-pocket expenses which are received by the school are treated as co-payments—effectively a tax—as they reduce the value of the education benefit and are payments that go into the fiscal system. [p200]

Expenses which go to the private sector, such as for uniforms or books, are excluded from the fiscal incidence analysis because they are not paid to a public entity and are not part of the fiscal system (even though they are legitimate expenses). [p200]
